subject.title: [Feature] Decouple dreaming from memory-core — allow any memory plugin to implement dreaming protocol

question: Should OpenClaw add a public dreaming provider/plugin-SDK contract, coordinate it with memory role-slot work, or leave dreaming orchestration plugin-owned through ClawHub?
rationale: Current source proves the requested protocol is missing, but adding it creates durable public config, SDK, scheduler, and memory-state semantics that automation should not choose.

options.title: Coordinate With Role Slots
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88504 as the architecture anchor, then design a small dreaming provider contract after the memory role taxonomy is accepted.

options.title: Separate Dreaming Protocol RFC
options.body: Keep this issue as the canonical RFC and ask for a smaller PR that only defines the dreaming provider surface, compatibility story, and proof matrix.

options.title: Keep Dreaming Plugin-Owned
options.body: Close this direction only if maintainers decide OpenClaw should not own generic dreaming orchestration and should point users to ClawHub plugins instead.

recommendation.title: Coordinate With Role Slots
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88504 as the architecture anchor, then design a small dreaming provider contract after the memory role taxonomy is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a project-level plugin/config API direction choice, and Peter Steinberger is listed as the project decision owner in CONTRIBUTING.md.
